title: pvXDMFReader
body:
## pvXDMFReader

Reads XDMF 2 files (.xmf/.xdmf): XML metadata with heavy arrays in HDF5. The output is the file's grid type (unstructured, structured or rectilinear) or a multiblock when it has several grids. Several file names form a file series read as time steps. Selections choose which grids, sets and point or cell arrays are loaded, and Stride subsamples structured grids. It is a distributed reader. pvXdmf3ReaderT and pvXdmf3ReaderS read XDMF 3 files.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The HDF5 file must stay where the XML references it, usually beside the .xmf file.
- Array, grid and set selections start from ParaView's choice; list them when later steps depend on particular names.
- Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

Native constructor: `XDMFReader`. Identity: `sources/XdmfReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the cell-centred arrays to load from the XDMF file. Arrays not listed are not read; the available names come from the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileNames` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `GridStatus` | Names of the grids to read when the file holds several grids (for example one per part or domain) in a collection. Unlisted grids are skipped; selecting a single grid can give a plain dataset instead of a multiblock. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the point-centred arrays to load from the XDMF file. Arrays not listed are not read, which saves memory and time; the available names come from the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `SetStatus` | Names of the XDMF sets (named groups of nodes, cells, faces or edges defined in the file, e.g. boundary patches) to load. Sets marked as ghost sets in the file cannot be selected. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Stride` | If loading structured data, this property indicate the number of indices per dimension (X, Y, or Z) to skip between each point included in this output. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvXDMFReader",
  "options": {
    "FileNames": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
